question.problem:
Find $\text{E}[X+3{Y}^{2}],$ given that random variables $X$ and $Y$ have the joint probability density function

$$
f(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{15},\, & 0\le x\le 3,\,\frac{x}{3}\le y\le 3; \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$
question.worked_solution:
Suppose $X$ and $Y$ are continuous random variables, and $f(x,y)$ is their joint probability density function. If $r:{R}^{2}\to R$ is a function of two variables, then the rule of the lazy statistician states that

$$
\text{E}[r(X,Y)]={∬}_{{R}^{2}}r(x,y)\,f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\text{d}y.
$$

In our case, we have

$$
r(x,y)=x+3{y}^{2}.
$$

Now, let's sketch the region $D=\{(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 3,\,\frac{x}{3}\le y\le 3\},$ where $f(x,y)$ is nonzero.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14161553/assets/bc454de7a5ef0a9b0e2620bb44a0d0b481638ca04905bf6d986a52715a95c3db.png)

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[X+3{Y}^{2}] & ={∬}_{{R}^{2}}(x+3{y}^{2})\,f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\text{d}y \\  & ={∬}_{D}(x+3{y}^{2})\,f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}{\int }_{x/3}^{3}(x+3{y}^{2})\cdot \frac{2}{15}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{2}{15}{\int }_{0}^{3}[xy+{y}^{3}]_{y=x/3}^{y=3}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{2}{15}{\int }_{0}^{3}[3x+27-\frac{{x}^{2}}{3}-\frac{{x}^{3}}{27}]\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{2}{15}{[\frac{3}{2}{x}^{2}+27x-\frac{{x}^{3}}{9}-\frac{{x}^{4}}{108}]}_{x=0}^{x=3} \\  & =\frac{2}{15}[\frac{27}{2}+81-3-\frac{3}{4}] \\  & =\frac{363}{30} \\  & =\frac{121}{10}.\end{aligned}
$$
